subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared notificationWake.reactions policy, a Telegram-specific reactionSemantics mapping, or a narrower per-message/action design for Telegram reaction-triggered turns?
rationale: The issue adds public wake/config semantics and operator-control behavior, while related open PRs implement competing API shapes that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt Shared Notification Wake
options.body: Use the queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical default-safe contract, then repair or replace that PR with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt Telegram Semantics Mapping
options.body: Use a Telegram-specific reactionSemantics shape if maintainers want per-emoji meanings before a cross-channel policy exists.

options.title: Defer Reaction Execution
options.body: Keep reactions passive for now and pause or close implementation candidates until the product surface is clearer.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Notification Wake
recommendation.body: Use the queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical default-safe contract, then repair or replace that PR with live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the open shared-policy candidate and has the strongest current history across the reaction, config, plugin-boundary, and product/API surfaces.
